requirements.obligation: Keep JS and Rust behavior aligned.
requirements.claimedEvidence: Partial. `scripts/runtime-parity.mjs` records what the JavaScript CLI prints (exit status, stdout, stderr) for all 125 repository RML sources in five modes (run, `--trace`, `extract js`, `extract rust`, `export rocq`) in `test-corpus/runtime-parity/observations.json` (625 observations, 29 targeted inputs covering E001–E067 diagnostics, equality layers, numeric formatting and extraction); `scripts/runtime-parity.test.mjs` checks the JavaScript CLI against it and rejects drift in status, output, coverage, sources and a live drifting second runtime, and `rust/tests/runtime_parity_tests.rs` runs the Rust `rml` binary over the same record. The comparison found and fixed divergences on both sides: `js/src/rml-links.mjs` (exponent-notation rounding NaN, eval-nat trace terms, Rocq export stack traces, E007/E009/E061 messages) and `rust/src/lib.rs`/`rust/src/rocq.rs` (named-lambda definitional equality, E003 operator definitions, declaration-error prefixes, Rocq inductive errors). Gap: `the Rust fixes and runtime_parity_tests.rs are compiled only by CI; other mirrored suites (for example portable-natural, rml-semantics) still assert less in Rust than in JavaScript, and parity is observed at the CLI, not proved`

requirements.claimedEvidence: `build-cache.test.mjs` rejects traversal/symlink escapes and external/source roots, protects tracked/preexisting/edited files, peer worktrees, nested clone source and uncommitted work, active outputs and acceptance evidence. Builders inside nested worktrees or repositories are attributed to their own tree unless they overlap this tree's caches; root aliases map custom targets; ancestor worktrees are not overlaps. On Linux and macOS a Node process started from the tree no longer defers cleanup when it runs a script file installed outside the tree, is not a package manager and holds no open file in the tree (for example a long-lived MCP server); an in-tree script, npm/npx/pnpm/yarn/corepack, a scriptless runner, an open tree file, a missing inventory or an unresolvable script still defer. `On Windows such a process still defers cleanup because no open-file inventory is read, and the symlink, ancestor-substitution and process-group safety tests run only on POSIX`.
